summary: Backend testing post repo-clone setup. 22/22 pytest tests pass covering auth (login cookies flags, /me, refresh, logout, brute-force 429), full CRUD for visitors/fleet/employees/directors/carregamentos/agendamentos, agendamento dar-entrada for visitante/frota/null km_saida, dashboard, reports, history, role permissions, 422 validation for empty-string on Optional[float]. Fixed 1 critical datetime timezone bug in auth brute-force check. Reported 1 medium-priority architectural bug: brute-force tracks by request.client.host which is the proxy/pod IP behind the K8s ingress + multi-pod backend, causing counts to split across pods/IPs (lockout only triggers after ~10 attempts total instead of 6).

minor.issue: Brute-force identifier uses request.client.host which resolves to the ingress/pod IP (10.64.130.9 / 10.64.129.166) behind the K8s load balancer. With 2 backend pods observed, attempts get distributed across pods and per-pod IP counters, so real-world lockout requires >6 attempts (saw ~10-12 before 429 triggered in multi-pod scenario). Should parse X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP header to get the real client IP and/or move brute-force state to MongoDB only (already in Mongo — the problem is only the identifier key).

fixed_during_testing.issue: TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes — MongoDB returned last_attempt as naive datetime but was compared with datetime.now(timezone.utc). This made the lockout branch throw 500 instead of returning 429 once count >= 5.
fixed_during_testing.fix: Added tzinfo=timezone.utc coercion when last_attempt lacks tzinfo before the subtraction.

action_items: Consider switching brute-force identifier from request.client.host to the first entry of X-Forwarded-For (or X-Real-IP), with a fallback to request.client.host, so the lockout is robust behind the K8s ingress and multiple backend pods. Acceptance: 6 consecutive wrong-password attempts from a single external client must return 429 (currently ~10-12 needed).
Optional: lower the lockout threshold to e.g. 3 per (ip,email) if stricter policy is desired (PRD originally mentioned 5).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1887 lines — should be split into routers (auth, visitors, fleet, employees, directors, carregamentos, agendamentos, dashboard, reports) under /app/backend/routers/ for maintainability.

Brute-force uses request.client.host directly; behind ingress this is the proxy IP. Also, the datetime coercion fix just applied is a symptom of not using tz-aware defaults consistently — consider normalizing all Mongo datetimes on write with timezone.utc.
All endpoints that call get_current_user also rely on check_role individually; a FastAPI dependency (Depends(require_roles([...]))) would DRY this pattern and reduce auth-bypass risk.
HTTPException messages are free-text strings. Consider a standard error envelope {code, message} for the frontend interceptor.
serialize_doc manually walks dicts; using a Pydantic response_model with from_attributes + a Mongo->dict mapper would be more robust.
seed_data_creation: Tests create TEST_ prefixed records and clean them up; residual test records removed via Mongo cleanup after the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is green (22/22). If frontend testing is requested next: use admin@portaria.com / admin123, backend URL https://access-control-251.preview.emergentagent.com. One open server-side note: brute-force lockout still uses request.client.host; if the frontend tries >5 wrong logins it may not trigger 429 in a single session due to multi-pod load-balancing — don't flag that as a blocker unless the main agent moves to X-Forwarded-For.
rca_of_the_issue: Two root causes found during login brute-force testing: (1) Mongo-stored last_attempt was naive (no tzinfo), but the subtraction in server.py:413 used tz-aware datetime.now(timezone.utc), raising TypeError after the counter reached >=5 — fixed by coercing tzinfo=UTC on read. (2) Brute-force identifier = f'{request.client.host}:{email}'. Behind the K8s ingress the observed client.host alternates between 10.64.130.9 and 10.64.129.166 (the two backend pods' peer addresses), so 5 sequential wrong attempts from one real client get split across 2+ identifier keys. Mitigation: parse the first IP from X-Forwarded-For header when present.
